P1.persona: Chef-rush — OSS visible from kitchen? Chef sees customer wait?
P1.top_finding: OSS is NOT mounted in the kitchen by default. Chef stays on KDS (/admin/kitchen-display-system). The two surfaces share the OrderStatusChanged broadcast pipeline so chef bump → customer column transition is real-time (Echo branch.{N} private channel + 5-15s polling fallback via OssSyncService). However, the OSS auto-scroll for >8 orders shows the chef NOTHING about queue depth: KDS has the N-HEAL-01 +N chip (Wave N 2026-05-24), OSS only has CSS oss-autoscroll keyframe. Chef can see urgency on his own KDS surface (chip + SLA color tier) but CANNOT verify customer wall is keeping up by glancing at it.
P1.rationale: Sync chain functional. Cross-surface visual parity (overflow chip) is asymmetric — chef has it, customer (and chef-by-proxy if they look at OSS) does not. Documented design choice but a real chef-rush kitchen who wants to verify customer perception lacks a quick affordance.

P2.persona: Client-impatient — ETA visible? Queue position? Notification ready?
P2.top_finding: Cross-validates B3-P2 finding: ZERO ETA propagation to OSS. CDSOrderDetailsResource exposes only 6 keys (id, order_serial_no, token, queue_number, order_type, status). No prep_time, no estimated_ready_at, no countdown. Client sees: (a) FIFO queue_number/token in PRÉPARATION column, (b) the same token migrates to PRÊT column with 10s visual window (oss-pop + oss-bounce + oss-pulse + oss-ready-flash). Audio chime is structurally muted on public wall (authBranchId<=0 gate at line 338 per GOAL Round 2 Impl C P0-OSS-01 2026-05-18). For an impatient client, the only timing signal is FIFO column position — no 'Prêt dans ~3 min', no progress bar.
P2.rationale: Design constraint (PII-free V1 minimal payload) is correct for compliance. But P2 client persona DOES feel the absence — V1.0.2 backlog candidate to add a non-PII ETA field (estimated_ready_at unix timestamp, no customer name leak) if owner wants to close P2 gap.

P3.persona: Caissier — can cashier see OSS state from POS?
P3.top_finding: YES — POS has dedicated pos-shortcuts__panel--ready widget (PosComponent.vue:268-337) that consumes the auth /api/admin/oss-order endpoint via PosShortcutOrderResource which exposes total in addition to the 6 CDS keys. Cashier sees N°{queue_number} + price + 'Livrer' CTA (data-testid='pos-shortcut-deliver-{id}'). Real-time refresh via _subscribeEcho (lines 2661-2718) listening to OrderCreated/OrderStatusChanged/OrderPaidAtCounter/ItemAvailabilityChanged/CatalogChanged. ONE GAP: OrderPaymentStatusChanged is NOT subscribed at WS layer; Stripe-refund payment status transitions surface only via REST polling (5-15s latency). Cash-counter flow uses OrderPaidAtCounter which IS subscribed (zero-latency).
P3.rationale: Cashier flow is well-covered for V1 (cash dominant in Le Cayenne). Stripe refund latency gap is real but P2 (refunds are rare, polling closes the gap within 15s).

P4.top_finding: OSS provides ZERO analytics. It is a real-time wall display only. NO orders-today count, NO throughput chart, NO avg prep time. An owner walking past at 22:00 sees only instantaneous PRÉPARATION/PRÊT state — empty columns = no signal about shift volume. Owner analytics live elsewhere (Z-report fiscal close + admin reports surfaces).
P4.rationale: Correct V1 separation of concerns. OSS = customer + cashier wall. Analytics = admin reports. Conflating them would clutter the wall and confuse the customer. No action needed.

P5.persona: Inspecteur-fiscal — PII compliance, customer data exposure
P5.top_finding: PII-free attestation HOLDS. Public endpoint /api/frontend/oss-order returns CDSOrderDetailsResource with 6 keys ONLY: id (int pk), order_serial_no (string), token (string short code), queue_number (int FIFO), order_type (int enum), status (int enum). Explicitly absent: customer_name, customer_phone, customer_email, customer_address, total, user_id. Source code line 67 attests: 'No PII (customer name/phone/address/total)'. Routes are physically separated (admin sanctum + permission vs frontend installed+apiKey+localization). NF525 audit chain unaffected (OrderStatusChanged → PersistOrderStatusChangedToOutbox listener writes to outbox; audit_logs HMAC chain preserved).
P5.rationale: GDPR-compliant wall display. No leak vector. The token+queue_number identifiers are low-cardinality and non-reversible. Even a passer-by photographing the wall reveals zero customer-identifiable information.

P6.persona: Staff-newbie — can staff easily understand OSS for customer questions?
P6.top_finding: Cognitive load is MINIMAL by design. Two color-coded columns (#B0004D red preparing / #1AB759 green ready). Single em-dash empty state (no jarring banners). 56px tokens readable at ≥3m. Transition animations (oss-pop + oss-bounce + oss-pulse + oss-ready-flash) give 10s attention window per Wave S-3 2026-05-20. WCAG 2.1 SC 2.3.3 compliance via prefers-reduced-motion media query (lines 480-488). A newbie can answer 'when ready?' from one glance: left=wait, right=pickup. No countdown to interpret, no jargon. Brand colors per CLAUDE.md flat doctrine.
P6.rationale: Onboarding cost ~30 seconds. The 2-column mental model is universal. Em-dash placeholder is honest and non-jarring. Wave S-3 typography optimizes for floor-staff scanning distance.
